about: Chord symbols as written: read, transposed (sharps or flats from the key), simplified, named in letters or solfège.

parseChord.about: A chord symbol read: its root, quality, seventh, extensions, alterations and bass; "N.C." is no chord; null when it isn't a chord.

nashvilleChord.about: A chord as a Nashville number in a key (issue #207): root and bass as degrees of the key, the rest as written; a minor key counts from its own tonic; the chord as written without a key.

romanChord.about: A chord as a Roman numeral in a key (issue #220): the root counted from the key's tonic, in capitals when major and lowercase when minor or diminished; ° diminished, ø half-diminished, + augmented; extensions as written; a slash chord's bass as a degree; a minor key counts from its own tonic; the chord as written without a key.

chordFamily.about: A chord's family, for colouring it (issue #9): major, minor, suspended, diminished, augmented or dominant (a major triad with a minor seventh); null for a power chord or something that isn't a chord.

chordTones.about: A chord's notes, each with its interval above the root, its pitch class (C = 0), its role and whether a shape may leave it out; null when it isn't a chord.

chordShapes.about: Shapes for a chord on a guitar (EADGBE unless a tuning is given) or a ukulele (GCEA, high G unless given), easiest and most usual first (issue #207): per string the fret (0 open, null muted), the fingers, barres, the fret the diagram starts at and the MIDI notes it sounds. Every needed note and nothing else; on a guitar the bass is lowest; at most four fingers, a barre counting as one. Each client draws them its own way (docs/chord-diagrams.md).

cases.name: ukulele with a low G: C

pianoVoicings.about: A chord's piano voicings (issue #207 phase 4): the right hand's notes in close position near middle C (MIDI 60), root position first then each inversion; the left hand's bass (the root, or a slash chord's bass) in the octave below - or the right hand only. Optional notes go when there'd be more than four.

songVoicings.about: Which voicing of each chord a song plays: smooth, the inversion nearest the chord before (the hand hardly moves), from the first chord's root position; or root position throughout.

cases.name: C G Am F, root position

progressionDegree.about: A chord as a degree for finding songs by progression (issue #204): its triad only - no 7ths, extensions or slash bass - as a Nashville number in the key.

songProgressions.about: Each section's progression in the song's key: chord changes in order, repeats collapsed; empty without a key.

checkChartChords.about: Chords that seem out of context (issue #356): outside the key and what songs in it often borrow, and rare in the song; or the only difference from every other section of its kind. Each with why and a suggestion; a key the chords mostly don't fit said once instead; a song without a key read in the one its chords fit.

progressionGrams.about: The runs of 3 and 4 chords in a song's sections, each section read as a loop, each run once: what songs are compared by.

parseProgressionQuery.about: A progression typed to search with, as degrees: numbers, Roman numerals (lowercase minor), flats and sharps; a plain 2, 3 or 6 is minor. Null when it isn't one.

findProgression.about: The sections whose chords, read as a loop, contain a progression in order.

progressionSimilarity.about: How alike two songs' runs are, 0 to 1: the shared ones over all, each weighted (here equally).

transitionProgressions.about: The ways from one song into the next (issues #10, #217, #218), from the song's last chord into the next one's first (its 1 when not given): V7 → I, ii7 V7 → I, V7sus V7 → I (those three recommended), an altered V7, a diminished vii°7, a chord both keys share, a chromatic bass, the backdoor iv7 ♭VII7, and the stacked bass + sus + altered - each with its usual form and variations, as degrees of the next song's key and spelled in it. `fast` keeps the one-chord forms.

chartEdgeChords.about: A chart's first and last chords as played (sounding), where a set's transition starts and leads; nulls without chords.

degreeChord.about: A degree of a key as a chord: a flat degree spelled with flats, a sharp one with sharps, the others as the key is. Null when it isn't a degree.

transitionDegrees.about: Chords typed for a transition, kept as degrees of the key it goes into; degrees typed are kept. Null when something isn't a chord or a degree.

voicingText.about: A voicing written down to keep a player's choice: left hand | right hand, as MIDI notes.

shapeText.about: A shape written as players write it: "x32010", a fret past 9 in parentheses.

transposeChord.about: A chord moved by semitones, spelt with sharps or flats as the target key uses; anything that isn't a chord is left as written.

keyUsesFlats.about: Whether chords in this key are spelt with flats.

formatChord.about: A chord named in letters ("english", as written) or solfège ("solfege": Do, Ré, Mi…).

simplifyChord.about: A chord made easier: only its triad (dropExtensions), without its bass note (dropBass).

chordBassOptions.about: A chord's bass notes (issue #228): root position, its inversions spelled from the chord, then the key's other notes walking up from its root.

sameChord.about: Whether two symbols are the same chord, however written.

diatonicChords.about: The chords of a key, I to vii, for the chord palette.
